spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN §11 (S11-infra-author)
LIVE STATE CAPTURED 2026-08-15 (read-only, aws s3api get-bucket-policy):
NoSuchBucketPolicy — this bucket has NO policy today. Rollback:
aws s3api delete-bucket-policy --bucket shramsafal-uploads-prod --region ap-south-1
=== ROUND 1 REVIEW FINDING C1 — FIX APPLIED 2026-08-15 ===
This file used to also carry a DenyUnencryptedUploads / DenyMissingEncryptionHeader
pair, justified as 'safe' because the bucket's DEFAULT encryption is AES256.
That justification was WRONG: default bucket encryption does not populate the
s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption CONDITION KEY — that key reflects the REQUEST
HEADER the writer sent, not what the bucket would apply by default. A Deny
with Null:{s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption:true} therefore denies every
PutObject that omits the header, REGARDLESS of whether default encryption
would have encrypted the object anyway — it is not the no-op it was claimed
to be. Two concrete hazards found:
1. No in-repo writer is confirmed for _deploy/, _deploys/, deploys/, or
apk/ on this bucket (grep across .github/, aws/, scripts/ finds no
s3 cp / s3 sync targeting shramsafal-uploads-prod; android-release.yml
pushes to a DIFFERENT bucket, shramsafal-app-prod). Something outside
this repo writes ~618 MB of deploy artifacts here. Plain `aws s3 cp`
sends no SSE header unless --sse is passed — this repo's own
aws/snapshot/snapshot.sh:245 proves the team knows to pass it, for a
DIFFERENT bucket. Whether the unaudited writer here does the same
cannot be determined from this repo.
2. s3:PutObject Deny with a Null SSE condition also denies UploadPart —
multipart parts structurally CANNOT carry an encryption header (it is
set once, at CreateMultipartUpload). Any object that crosses the
multipart threshold — plausible for the 44 MB tarballs in _deploy/ —
would be denied even when the initiator set the header correctly at
initiation.
This cannot be settled by reading this repo (it needs CloudTrail data events
or a full enumeration of every principal/pipeline capable of writing here).
Per this review round's explicit instruction, it is NOT reclassified as
'prove it' work for this lane — it is moved to the same do-not-apply-yet
posture as the raw bucket's CMK deny rail:
aws/uploads/bucket-policy-encryption-deny.NOT-VERIFIED-DO-NOT-APPLY.json
See that file for what must be verified before it can be applied, and for
the exact statements (unchanged in substance, only moved).
WHAT REMAINS IN THIS FILE: TLS-only enforcement (DenyInsecureTransport).
This has none of the above hazards — aws:SecureTransport is a TLS-layer
property of the connection itself, not a per-request header a writer can
forget to set, so there is no 'unaudited writer might not send it' failure
mode and no multipart interaction (every S3 API action, including
UploadPart, either uses TLS or it doesn't; there is nothing to omit).
APPLY (founder only): aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket shramsafal-uploads-prod --policy file://bucket-policy.json --region ap-south-1
(apply-config.sh does this as part of the single transaction.)
VERIFY: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket shramsafal-uploads-prod --region ap-south-1 | jq -r '.Policy | fromjson | .Statement[].Sid'
